newsitem.title: GERMANY: Analysts to put Deutsche Telekom on hold.
newsitem.headline: Analysts to put Deutsche Telekom on hold.

text.p: German phone giant Deutsche Telekom, which recently launched Europe's largest ever initial public offering, is about to experience the fickle winds of the market as analysts are set to downgrade its stock next week.

Telecommunications analysts of Telekom's underwriting banks, not allowed to publish research or comment on the stock until Friday, said they already had or were about to change their previous recommendation for the stock to hold from buy.

Explaining their decisions, analysts cited the high price of Telekom's listing and said investors were getting ready for France Telecom's listing and the privatisation of Telefonica of Spain. Those two companies alone are expected to float $9 billion worth of stock later this year.
"We changed our recommendation to hold from buy today," Oliver Ehrenberg, London-based telecommunications analyst for Flemings Securities told Reuters.
A telecoms analyst at HSBC James Capel said the investment bank has had Telekom on its hold list since the November issue.
Analysts from the global coordinators of Telekom's share listing -- Deutsche Bank AG, Dresdner Bank AG and Goldman Sachs -- either declined comment or could not be reached on Friday.
Analysts at Morgan Stanley, Merrill Lynch and CS First Boston said they had not initiated coverage of the stock yet and declined comment until next week.

While Germany's DAX index has been soaring to record highs, shares in Deutsche Telekom have underperformed the list of 30 blue-chips by 16 percent since its listing on November 18 and some analysts said there was more pressure on the downside.
Telekom's initial public offering was priced at 28.50 marks and the first trading price was registered at 32.20 marks.

Telekom shares have backed off earlier highs and fallen sharply this week, dipping below the opening price on Tuesday and closing at 30.52 marks on Friday, down 5.2 percent from the November 18 opening, but still 7.1 percent above the IPO price.

"Our recommendation has been to take profits at anything significantly above 30 marks," said Nicole Cousins, telecoms analyst at Bank Julius Baer in Frankfurt. "We still feel 30 marks is a fair value." Julius Baer also has Telekom on hold.
While it is still too soon to judge the new share's performance, analysts expect Telekom stock to get its first test of strength over the coming weeks and months.

"In the medium term Telekom shares will tend to go back to around the issue price because investors want to see what happens when it gets to around that level," said Ehrenberg. "By medium term, I mean the next three to six months."

Many analysts and fund managers thought Telekom's IPO price was too high and left little room for short-term gains. Investors are also gearing up for a new round of privatisations of European telecoms companies.
Analysts also noted that German bond yields were rising, dulling the attraction of shares as the difference to dividend yields narrows.

There are also more attractive telecoms stocks available in Europe. Shares in Telefonica of Spain have risen 18 percent since Deutsche Telekom's share launch and 96 percent since the beginning of January 1996 to 3,250 pesatas on Friday.
Shares in Mannesmann, a main Telekom rival, have risen 8.2 percent since Telekom's listing and 45.5 percent since the beginning of 1996 to 673.50 marks.
"After the Telekom issue, Mannesmann was always the one to buy in Germany and not Deutsche Telekom," said London-based telecoms analyst Paul Ryb.
